bland|politic.distinction: Bland means without flavour or edge, while politic means shrewdly judged for the circumstances, which is praise rather than complaint.

bland|vapid.distinction: Bland is inoffensively flat, while vapid adds emptiness of mind to the flatness.

blatant|clamorous.distinction: Blatant is wrongdoing done openly and without shame, while clamorous is loud insistent noise.

blatant|flagrant.distinction: Blatant stresses that no attempt was made to hide it, while flagrant stresses how badly the rule was broken.

blatant|vociferous.distinction: Blatant describes shameless openness, while vociferous describes sheer volume in expressing a view.

bogus|phony.distinction: Bogus and phony both mean fake; bogus attaches to the counterfeit article, phony more often to the insincere person.

boisterous|unruly.distinction: Boisterous is cheerful noisy energy, while unruly is a refusal to be controlled.

bombastic|orotund.distinction: Bombastic is inflated language with nothing behind it, while orotund is the rounded booming delivery of it.

bombastic|turgid.distinction: Bombastic swells the language to impress, while turgid swells it until the sense is lost in the heaviness.

bowdlerize|expurgate.distinction: Bowdlerize and expurgate both cut the offending passages; bowdlerize names the prudish editor who did it to Shakespeare.

bridle|bristle.distinction: Bridle is drawing oneself up in offence, while bristle is the sudden prickling anger of an animal raising its hair.

broach|brooch.distinction: Broach opens a subject for discussion, while a brooch is an ornamental pin, and only the spelling separates them.

broadside|tirade.distinction: A broadside is one heavy attack delivered at once, while a tirade is a long angry speech that keeps going.

bromide|platitude.distinction: A bromide is a stale remark offered to soothe, while a platitude is any worn truism passed off as wisdom.

browbeat|hector.distinction: Browbeat bullies by intimidation and threat, while hector bullies by nagging insistent talk.

bucolic|pastoral.distinction: Bucolic and pastoral both paint country life as pleasant; pastoral also covers shepherds and the poems written about them.

byzantine|convoluted.distinction: Byzantine complexity is devious and full of intrigue, while convoluted complexity is merely tangled.

byzantine|tortuous.distinction: Byzantine suggests scheming behind the complexity, while tortuous is the twisting winding path itself.

cabal|conjure.distinction: A cabal is a small group plotting in secret, while conjure summons something up as if by magic.

cabal|conspire.distinction: A cabal is the group of plotters, while conspire is the act of plotting that such a group carries on.

cabal|faction.distinction: A cabal plots in secret, while a faction is an open dissenting group inside a larger body.

cabal|machinate.distinction: A cabal is the secret group itself, while machinate is the scheming that group spends its time on.

cacophony|clamor.distinction: Cacophony is harsh clashing sound, while clamor is loud noise that carries a demand in it.

cacophony|din.distinction: Cacophony is discordant and grating, while a din is simply loud and continuous.

cadaverous|gaunt.distinction: Gaunt is thin and hollowed by hardship, while cadaverous goes further and makes the person look like a corpse.

cajole|coax.distinction: Cajole works by flattery and persistence, while coax works by gentle patience and can be entirely honest.

cajole|inveigle.distinction: Cajole flatters someone into agreeing, while inveigle adds deceit and lures them somewhere they would not have gone.

cajole|wheedle.distinction: Cajole and wheedle both flatter someone into yielding; wheedle is the softer, more childlike coaxing of the two.

calumny|obloquy.distinction: Calumny is the false accusation itself, while obloquy is the public condemnation that lands on the person afterwards.

calumny|slander.distinction: Calumny is the malicious falsehood in general, while slander is the spoken form of it and an actionable wrong.

candidness|candor.distinction: Candidness and candor name the same honesty; candor is the usual form in formal writing and candidness the rarer one.

candid|forthright.distinction: Candid is honesty about what one really thinks, while forthright is directness in saying it without evasion.

cantankerous|ornery.distinction: Cantankerous is quarrelsome bad temper, while ornery adds a stubborn refusal to cooperate.

cant|jargon.distinction: Cant is insincere moralising talk, while jargon is the technical vocabulary of a trade that outsiders cannot follow.

capricious|erratic.distinction: Capricious changes come from whim, while erratic ones follow no pattern at all and need no motive.

capricious|fickle.distinction: Capricious is sudden change of any kind, while fickle is specifically change of loyalty or affection.

castigate|chastise.distinction: Castigate and chastise both rebuke severely; chastise can extend to actual punishment, castigate stays in words.

castigate|objurgate.distinction: Castigate is the common word for severe rebuke, while objurgate is its rarer and more formal twin.

caustic|mordant.distinction: Caustic wit burns whoever it lands on, while mordant wit bites with a dry ironic edge.

caustic|vitriolic.distinction: Caustic is sharp and corrosive in tone, while vitriolic is savage enough to be meant as an attack.

cede|concede.distinction: Cede hands over territory or power formally, while concede admits a point or gives up a contest.

cede|relinquish.distinction: Cede is the formal transfer of territory or right, while relinquish is any letting go of what one held.

chagrin|humble.distinction: Chagrin is the distress felt at being humiliated, while humble is the act of bringing someone's pride down.

chagrin|humiliate.distinction: Chagrin is what the victim feels, while humiliate is what somebody else does to produce it.

chagrin|mortify.distinction: Chagrin is the vexed disappointment felt, while mortify is the deeper shame inflicted from outside.

chastise|objurgate.distinction: Chastise can mean punish as well as scold, while objurgate stays entirely in the realm of stinging words.

chauvinism|jingoism.distinction: Chauvinism is blind loyalty to one's own group of any kind, while jingoism is that loyalty turned warlike toward other nations.

chauvinist|jingoist.distinction: A chauvinist believes their own group superior, while a jingoist wants the nation to prove it by force.

chicanery|guile.distinction: Chicanery is trickery in the details of a scheme, while guile is the cunning in the person who runs it.

choleric|irascible.distinction: Choleric and irascible both name a quick temper; choleric comes from the old humours and suggests a hot constitution.

circumvent|elude.distinction: Circumvent gets round a rule or obstacle by cleverness, while elude slips out of a grasp that was closing on you.

circumvent|evade.distinction: Circumvent finds a way round the obstacle, while evade dodges the thing coming at you.

circumvent|hedge.distinction: Circumvent gets round a requirement entirely, while hedge simply avoids committing so the risk stays limited.

clamorous|vociferous.distinction: Clamorous is the noise of a crowd insisting, while vociferous is one voice raised loudly to be heard.

clamor|din.distinction: Clamor is loud noise with a demand inside it, while a din is noise and nothing more.

clandestine|surreptitious.distinction: Clandestine describes an operation planned in secrecy, while surreptitious describes an act done stealthily in the moment.

cleave|cohere.distinction: Cleave means both to split and to cling, while cohere only holds things together, which is why cleave is the trap.

cloying|treacly.distinction: Cloying is sweetness that sickens by excess, while treacly names the thick sticky sentimentality doing it.

coalesce|conflate.distinction: Coalesce is separate things growing into one whole, while conflate is confusing two distinct things that should have stayed apart.

coax|inveigle.distinction: Coax persuades gently and openly, while inveigle persuades by flattery and deceit.

coax|wheedle.distinction: Coax is patient gentle persuasion, while wheedle lays on the flattery to get its way.

coddle|cosset.distinction: Coddle and cosset both mean pampering; coddle carries more suggestion that the care is making the person soft.

codicil|rider.distinction: A codicil is an addition to a will, while a rider is a clause attached to a contract or a bill.

colossal|prodigious.distinction: Colossal is sheer physical size, while prodigious is scale impressive enough to astonish.

commence|start.distinction: Commence means to begin, while the tested sense of start is to jump in surprise, which is the trap in the pair.

commendable|laudable.distinction: Commendable and laudable both mean deserving praise; laudable more often praises the intention where commendable praises the act.

commit|consecrate.distinction: Commit pledges oneself or carries out an act, while consecrate sets something apart as sacred.

complaisance|deference.distinction: Complaisance is eagerness to please anyone, while deference is submission to someone's authority or judgement.

complaisant|obliging.distinction: Complaisant yields to others to keep them happy, while obliging goes out of its way to help them.

conciliate|mollify.distinction: Conciliate wins an opponent round to agreement, while mollify only takes the heat out of their anger.

conciliate|pacify.distinction: Conciliate brings an opponent round to agreement, while pacify only quiets them down, sometimes by force.

conciliate|placate.distinction: Conciliate aims at genuine reconciliation, while placate just buys off the anger with a concession.

conciliate|reconcile.distinction: Conciliate is the effort to win someone over, while reconcile is the restored agreement that effort is aiming at.

concomitant|incidental.distinction: Concomitant runs alongside the main thing as a companion, while incidental attaches to it as a minor by-product.

condemn|decry.distinction: Condemn passes judgement, sometimes a formal sentence, while decry loudly denounces something in public.

condemn|denounce.distinction: Condemn declares something wrong, while denounce names and attacks it publicly.

condemn|excoriate.distinction: Condemn states the judgement, while excoriate delivers it savagely enough to strip the skin.

condemn|objurgate.distinction: Condemn is the verdict on the thing, while objurgate is the furious scolding aimed at a person.

conduct|deportment.distinction: Conduct is what a person does, while deportment is how they carry and present themselves while doing it.

conjure|conspire.distinction: Conjure summons something up as if by magic, while conspire plots secretly with others.

conjure|entreat.distinction: Conjure calls something into being, while entreat asks a person earnestly and humbly for something.

conjure|evoke.distinction: Conjure produces something as if from nothing, while evoke calls up a feeling or memory already there.

conjure|invoke.distinction: Conjure summons a thing into existence, while invoke calls on an authority or power for support.

conjure|machinate.distinction: Conjure produces something as if by magic, while machinate works out a scheme in secret.

consecrate|ordain.distinction: Consecrate sets a thing or person apart as sacred, while ordain confers an office or lays down a decree.

conspire|machinate.distinction: Conspire is plotting together with others, while machinate is the scheming itself and needs no accomplice.

constant|incessant.distinction: Constant means unchanging and can be a virtue, while incessant means it never pauses and is usually a complaint.

constant|perpetual.distinction: Constant is steady and unvarying, while perpetual is endless in time.

constant|unremitting.distinction: Constant describes something steady, while unremitting describes pressure that never once lets up.

constrict|contract.distinction: Constrict narrows something by squeezing it, while contract shrinks it overall, and can also mean catching an illness.

consummate|virtuoso.distinction: Consummate describes skill that is complete in every part, while a virtuoso is the person whose technique dazzles.

contempt|despite.distinction: Contempt is the scorn felt, while despite is its older form and now survives mainly in the phrase in despite of.

contempt|disdain.distinction: Contempt is scorn for what is beneath notice, while disdain is the haughty refusal to stoop to it.

contempt|scorn.distinction: Contempt is the settled low opinion, while scorn is that opinion expressed openly and with heat.

contrite|penitent.distinction: Contrite is the crushed feeling of regret, while penitent adds the intention to atone for what was done.

contrived|stilted.distinction: Contrived means artificially forced into being, while stilted means stiff and unnatural in how it comes out.

conundrum|enigma.distinction: A conundrum is a problem that puzzles the reason, while an enigma is a person or thing that resists being understood at all.

convoluted|tortuous.distinction: Convoluted is folded in on itself and hard to follow, while tortuous twists and turns along its whole length.

cordial|genial.distinction: Cordial is warmth shown to someone, while genial is a cheerful good humour in the person themselves.

cornucopia|profusion.distinction: A cornucopia is the overflowing abundance pictured as a horn of plenty, while profusion is simply a great quantity poured out.
